artworks.title: Landscape with Hypsipyle and Opheltes
artworks.description: Johann Christian Reinhart's classical landscape at the Staatliche Kunsthalle Karlsruhe sets the Lemnian queen Hypsipyle in an Arcadian Nemean wilderness with the infant Opheltes (Archemoros). The painting freezes the quiet before the snake-strike that will found the Nemean Games — Hypsipyle as nurse and tragic witness rather than Argonaut queen.

artworks.title: Stone figurine of Hypsipyle with Opheltes
artworks.description: An eroded stone figurine from the shrine of the hero Opheltes at Nemea, now in the Archaeological Museum of Nemea, shows a woman — almost certainly Hypsipyle — holding a child to her breast. Late Archaic or early Classical in date, it is among the rare cult objects that place the Lemnian exile at the heart of the Nemean hero-cult she accidentally founded.

artworks.title: Hypsipyle Finds Opheltes Killed by a Snake
artworks.description: Karl Ludwig Friedrich Becker's mural for the Niobidensaal of Berlin's Neues Museum (destroyed) staged the instant Hypsipyle discovers the infant Opheltes slain by a serpent — the catastrophe that turns a forgotten Lemnian nurse into the aetiology of the Nemean Games. The surviving reproduction keeps the nineteenth-century museum's reading of her as a figure of horrified recognition.

artworks.title: Opheltes Ensnared by the Snake
artworks.description: A nineteenth-century line reconstruction after an ancient bas-relief, published by K. A. Baumeister, shows the infant Opheltes (Archemoros) strangled in the coils of the Nemean serpent — the death Hypsipyle failed to prevent when she left the child to guide the Seven against Thebes to a spring. The print preserves the visual type through which Hypsipyle's Nemean tragedy entered modern handbooks.

films.title: Jason and the Argonauts
films.description: Hallmark's miniseries keeps the Lemnian stop: Hypsipyle's island of women, and the queen who takes Jason before the Argo sails on for the fleece.

music.title: Giasone
music.description: Cavalli's Venetian hit makes Hypsipyle a principal rival to Medea — the Lemnian queen who loves Jason and nearly loses everything to Colchian magic.
